studies.Authors: Cho E, Giovannucci EL, Joh HK
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Diet was assessed repeatedly using a validated semi-quantitative food-frequency questionnaire in both studies.

sample_size.excerpt: During follow-up of 24 years among 77,208 women (918,891 person-years) and 22 years among 47,886 men (1,731,752 person-years), we accrued 436 cases of RCC (225 women and 211 men).
sample_size.location: Results, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 77208 + 47886 = 125094

cases.excerpt: During follow-up of 24 years among 77,208 women (918,891 person-years) and 22 years among 47,886 men (1,731,752 person-years), we accrued 436 cases of RCC (225 women and 211 men).

comparison.excerpt: Participants were grouped based on dietary intake quintiles. Relative risks (RRs) of RCC (and 95% confidence invervals [CIs]) for quintiles of nutrients were calculated.

design.excerpt: We conducted prospective follow-up studies of women in the Nurses’ Health Study and men in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study.
